origin.description: Pearson chi-square test of the composite hypothesis of normality.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Numeric vector. Missing values are dropped.

arguments.name: n.classes
arguments.text: Number of equiprobable classes. The default uses n after missing values are dropped.

arguments.name: adjust
arguments.text: If TRUE, the chi-square reference has n.classes - 3 degrees of freedom. If FALSE, it has n.classes - 1.

origin.details: Observations are counted in classes formed from the normal cdf of the raw values, using the sample mean and sample standard deviation. A standard deviation of 0 makes pnorm return 0 or 1, so those points fall outside the classes and the statistic is n. A non-positive degrees of freedom makes pchisq warn and return NA.
origin.value: An htest list with statistic P, the p-value, the method, the data name, n.classes, and df.

translation.description: Pearson chi-square test of the composite hypothesis of normality.

arguments.name: n_classes
arguments.text: Number of equiprobable classes. None uses ceiling(2 * n^(2/5)) after missing values are dropped.

arguments.name: adjust
arguments.text: If True, the chi-square reference has n_classes - 3 degrees of freedom. If False, it has n_classes - 1.

translation.details: Observations are counted in classes formed from the normal cdf of the raw values, using the sample mean and sample standard deviation. A standard deviation of 0 makes pnorm return 0 or 1, so those points fall outside the classes and the statistic is n. A non-positive degrees of freedom warns and returns NaN. The chi-square tail is SciPy.
translation.value: An htest object with statistic P, the p-value, the method, the data name, n_classes, and df.
translation.example:
from nortest import pearson_test

x = [2.1, 3.4, float("nan"), 1.2, 5.6, 4.0, 3.3, 2.8, 6.1, 1.9, float("nan"), 4.4]
print(pearson_test(x), end="")
